newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania road tax decree clears parliament.
newsitem.headline: Romania road tax decree clears parliament.

text.p: A government decree setting up a road tax that has been fiercely opposed by car makers, importers and irate motorists won parliamentary approval on Wednesday, clearing the way for a campaign to patch up Romania's potholed highways.
The government hopes to raise $183 million each year for repairs badly needed to 70 percent of the country's 14,500-km (9,000-mile) road network.
The decree, redrafted with lower assessments, was endorsed by the parliament's upper house, the Senate, after the Chamber of Deputies had passed it last month.

Under the revised bill, vehicles with engines of up to 1,500 cc are assessed the equivalent of $7 annually and middle-range cars at double that amount in a country where average monthly wages stand at less than $80.

Owners of vehicles exceeding 3,200 cc will have to pay an annual $85. The law's original version slapped much higher fees on the medium-sized cars, sparking noisy "go-slow" protests by drivers in major cities and criticism by car manufacturers which said the tax would kill their businesses.
According to official statistics, 1.6 million cars of up to 1,500 ccs are registered in the country of 22 million, along with about one million vehicles exceeding that capacity.
